title: Where Medicaid Renewals Meet IT Reality
summary: Unified visibility helps state agencies protect critical digital services by linking citizen experience to network, application, and infrastructure performance for faster troubleshooting and improved service reliability.
body_markdown:
[State agencies](https://www.netscout.com/industries/government/state-local) need more than isolated dashboards when critical citizen services are on the line. They need a unified way to see service impact, trace the full transaction path, and act before access to benefits is disrupted.


For Medicaid members, renewals are not just another online transaction. A slow portal, failed login, or timeout near a deadline can affect access to healthcare benefits, increase call center pressure, and create frustration for members, providers, and caseworkers. For the IT teams supporting these services, the challenge is just as urgent: Find the cause quickly, coordinate across teams, and keep the digital front door open.


That is exactly the kind of challenge explored in the Four Inc.-hosted webinar “[Unified Visibility for State Government: Insights from Grafana and NETSCOUT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TBU80ZxY_Dw) .” The discussion shows how combining Grafana Labs’ visualization capabilities with NETSCOUT’s packet-derived service assurance can help agencies eliminate blind spots across hybrid cloud, network, and application environments.


## The Problem: Healthy Tools, Unhealthy Experiences


A Medicaid renewal environment is typically made up of many interconnected systems (the member portal, authentication, DNS, APIs, eligibility engines, databases, firewalls, data centers, cloud services, and network infrastructure). While each team may have its own monitoring view and each tool may show that its individual domain looks healthy, citizens may still be experiencing failed transactions or unacceptable delays.


In these scenarios, the agency’s biggest obstacle is not the lack of data but rather a lack of shared context. Without a complete view of the transaction path, teams can lose valuable time debating whether the source of the slowdown is the portal, the network, a firewall, an API, a back-end eligibility system, a cloud dependency, or simply unprecedented demand.


## The Solution: One Operational Picture, Deeper Evidence Underneath


In the illustrative Medicaid renewal scenario, Grafana Labs and NETSCOUT work together to give agency teams a unified service-assurance view. Grafana Labs brings operational telemetry together in a shared dashboard, helping teams visualize transaction volumes, availability, errors, latency, service maps, and alerts. NETSCOUT adds the packet-derived network, application, location, and service-level evidence needed to understand what is happening beneath the dashboard.


Together, those capabilities connect the citizen experience to the services supporting each renewal transaction, from the first click in the portal through authentication, APIs, eligibility systems, databases, and hybrid infrastructure. Instead of chasing separate alerts, teams can follow the service path, correlate demand with application and network behavior, and identify whether the impact is statewide or concentrated in a specific location or dependency.


## Why It Matters for State Government IT


For[public sector](https://www.netscout.com/industries/government) organizations, digital service performance is directly tied to trust. Citizens expect online services to work, especially when the service affects healthcare, benefits, licensing, taxes, or other essential needs. When agencies can see the full picture across networks, clouds, applications, and users, they are better positioned to protect the experience people depend on.


- A single operational view across transaction volume, service performance, applications, networks, locations, and dependencies
- Faster isolation of whether a slowdown is tied to the portal, network, firewall, eligibility engine, API, backend system, or traffic surge
- Shared evidence that helps application, network, cloud, infrastructure, and service teams work from the same picture
- Earlier visibility into emerging service degradation so teams can act before more people are unable to complete critical transactions
- More consistent access to digital services during periods of peak demand


### Watch the Webinar to See the Full Story


The Medicaid renewal example is just one way to think about the broader value of unified visibility for state government. In the webinar, experts from Grafana Labs and NETSCOUT discuss how agencies can reduce monitoring silos, accelerate troubleshooting, support hybrid cloud modernization, and improve the digital front-door experience citizens interact with every day.


If your organization is working to modernize critical services, reduce blind spots, or improve confidence during high-demand events, this session is worth watching. You will come away with practical ideas for building a single source of truth across agency networks, clouds, applications, and digital services.
